sentenceSets.sentence: A staunch supporter of the initiative, she continued making the case after many who had started alongside her had moved to other priorities.

answerChoices.reasoning: Passionate describes intense emotional commitment, whereas staunch specifically implies steadfast loyalty that persists even when others abandon the cause.
Enthusiastic describes eager interest, whereas staunch emphasizes unwavering loyalty through time when others have lost interest.
Devoted suggests deep commitment, but staunch specifically emphasizes the quality of remaining loyal when others have moved on.
Principled describes adherence to moral beliefs, whereas staunch specifically emphasizes continued loyalty to a particular cause over time.
Determined describes resolve to achieve a goal, whereas staunch emphasizes loyalty to a person or principle specifically.
Loyal and staunch overlap significantly, but staunch carries the specific implication of maintaining loyalty when others have abandoned it.
Sincere describes genuine belief, whereas staunch emphasizes lasting loyalty despite changing circumstances.
Committed describes dedication, but staunch specifically emphasizes the persistence of that dedication when others give up.
Fickle describes changing loyalties and interests, which is the opposite of the steadfast consistency that staunch implies.
Ambivalent means uncertain or conflicted, which contradicts the unwavering loyalty conveyed by staunch.
Hesitant suggests uncertainty and reluctance, the opposite of the confident unwavering commitment that staunch conveys.

sentenceSets.sentence: The staunch competitor refused to acknowledge fatigue or injury, pushing through pain that would have stopped most athletes.
